A scratch test (deleted afterwards) showed the merge-words defect listed under blocking.

blocking.issue: recall words a done task's merge differently from its merge record and from the chat's own '# Your files' facts. For a pull request closed without merging it says "Its pull request waits for your Merge." It also says nothing for left_to_you or merging records that the person did approve. This breaks the area's decision "one status map and one place per fact: chat never says what a screen contradicts" (design §5 rules 9 and 10) on exactly the question U-092 checks ('when was the README merged?'). Run L3's live-check repository had closed pull requests, so this state is real.
blocking.evidence: mergeWords returns 'merged on …' for state merged and 'merges when its checks pass' for waiting_checks. Otherwise, for any done task with approval 'none', it returns 'waits for your Merge', whatever the state and last_outcome. loop/merge.ts:1178-1182 records a closed pull request as state left_to_you with last_outcome 'closed' and sentence 'PR #N was closed without merging.' project-facts.ts:549-577 classifies that record as closed, and uses the record's sentence for left_to_you and for merging. My scratch test (a done task 'Write the FAQ' whose record was moved to left_to_you / closed) got this from recall {words:'FAQ', kinds:['tasks']}: 'r1 [task, Wed 11 Nov, Quote Page, strong] Write the FAQ: Done. Its pull request waits for your Merge.' The CR-2 test only covers merged and queued+none.
blocking.expected: recall's merge words follow the same classification the facts use: merged (with its date), closed without merging, waiting for your Merge with the record's sentence, or merging by itself with the record's sentence. Best is to share one function with project-facts.ts' repositoryFacts so there is one place per fact. Write a failing composed case first (a closed pull request, and a left_to_you record after a Merge), then the fix, then the sibling in recall_open's taskText.

non_blocking: The fixer's note to C3 says onStep receives stepLine for every read, recall and command tool. Command tools never call onStep (agent.ts registers commands.tools without it), so 'Preparing the change…' and 'Keeping that for later…' exist only in the unit test. Correct the note, or wire it in C3.

docs/user-guide.md (Chat, 'Ask about anything recorded') says 'While it looks it says what it is doing ("Looking through last week's sessions…")'. Nothing shows the step lines until d1109-chat-depth (C3) draws onStep, so until C3 merges this is a promise the app does not keep (§5 rule 9).

Sources' links: the conversation outside any project links to '/talk', which is not a route (routes.tsx has no talk; NotFoundPage). '/inbox?answered=', '/inbox?request=', '/projects/:id?decision=' and '/changes?projectId=' are not read by those pages; only Tasks ?task= and Files ?path= are. C3's From line needs these handled.

The merge date comes from merge_record.updated_at (recall.ts:487). A later patch, such as the take-out pull request's state, moves that date. A merged record whose work was taken out still reads 'merged on …'.
STATUS_DOC_RE is duplicated in recall.ts:890 instead of documents going 'through agent.ts's own loader' as the spec says. The regex is the same, so behaviour does not differ.

Sessions on one day all read 'The session of Sun 15 Nov' in hits and sources (four identical titles on the bench); only the open has the time. Add the time when two sessions share a day, so the From line and the model can tell them apart.

Bench fidelity: the role-player passes the whole line as words and opens r1 even when every hit is weak. So the 'say what you looked through' path appears only when nothing matches at all; 'pizza oven' got 'From the record: Task "Write the guide"…' via the filler word 'say'/'says'. Consider having recallPlay treat all-weak as nothing found. Live check 4 must check the real model's no-match wording.

Card hits on multi-question cards cut the answer at 160 characters before the later answers. snippetOf centres on the first query term, not the rarest, so 'opening hours' only showed through the decision hit.
Per-search N+1 store reads: mergeRecord.forTask per done task (up to 10,000 tasks), sessionRowView per session, statSync per document. Fine for small homes; watch the chat latency on a large one.
Spending sums the whole project ledger; in a shared project another person's chat counts as 'the work'.

recall_open of a task returns task_get's existing run lines with raw ISO timestamps ('Run (review, critic, 2026-11-15T18:22:13.777Z)'). They are model-facing and moved, not new; a local date would match the rest of recall.
CR-9's 700-token bound: the measured +~1,050 tokens on a status turn is in not_done with sound evidence; the session lead decides.
